chunks.text: The mango tree (Mangifera indica) belongs to the genus Mangifera and is believed to have originated in the border region of what is now Bangladesh, northeastern India and Myanmar, from where it spread across South and Southeast Asia in ancient times. Arab and Persian traders carried it to East Africa around the 9th-10th centuries, and Portuguese sailors later spread it to Brazil, the Caribbean and Mexico; it did not reach Florida until 1833. Genetic studies show a complex domestication history with two distinct populations — a subtropical Indian group with monoembryonic seeds and a tropical Southeast Asian group with polyembryonic seeds — and over 500 cultivars are grown worldwide today. Mature trees can reach 30-40 metres tall with crowns 10-15 metres across, and some specimens are still fruiting after 300 years. The fruit has a single flattened stone, waxy skin that ranges from green to yellow-red or purple when ripe, and weighs anywhere from about 140 grams to 2 kilograms; the pulp is roughly 84% water and 15% carbohydrate. Contact with the sap, leaves or skin can cause dermatitis in sensitive people because mango is related to poison ivy.

Ripe mango is eaten fresh across Asia, while raw, unripe fruit is used in Indian pickles and chutneys such as avakaya. Popular Indian preparations include aam panna, a raw-mango summer drink, and mango lassi, a yoghurt-based drink. Southeast Asian cuisines use green mango in salads dressed with fish sauce or vinegar, and Filipino cuisine uses ripe mango in desserts like mango float. The mango is the national fruit of India, Pakistan and the Philippines, and the national tree of Bangladesh. Mango flowers and leaves are used in Hindu worship of Saraswati during Vasant Panchami and in Ganesh Chaturthi decorations, and the Jain goddess Ambika is traditionally depicted seated under a mango tree; the classical Sanskrit poet Kalidasa also praised the fruit. Paisley motifs on textiles are named after the shape of an unripe mango in several Indian languages. In 2023, global mango production reached about 61 million tonnes, with India alone producing roughly 43% of the world total; the Alphonso cultivar is often called the 'king of mangoes,' while Tommy Atkins dominates Western export markets.
